newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: War crimes judges weigh Srebrenica killer's appeal.
newsitem.headline: War crimes judges weigh Srebrenica killer's appeal.

text.p: Judges at the U.N. war crimes tribunal on Monday adjourned a hearing on a Croat's appeal against his sentence of 10 years in jail for killing Bosnian Moslems at Srebrenica.
Drazen Erdemovic last November became the first person to be sentenced by an international war crimes tribunal since the Nuremberg and Tokyo trials after World War Two.

Erdemovic, who served in the Bosnian Serb army despite being a Croat, confessed to killing unarmed Moslems from the U.N. "safe haven" of Srebrenica in eastern Bosnia in July 1995, saying he would have been killed had he not joined in the executions.
Thousands of Moslem men and boys went missing after the fall of Srebrenica, believed to have been systematically murdered by victorious Bosnian Serbs.
Former Bosnian Serb President Radovan Karadazic and his military commander Ratko Mladic have been indicted in their absence by the U.N. tribunal for war crimes at Srebrenica.

Erdemovic appealed in December against his sentence, with lawyers arguing that some facts were insufficiently established, the killings had not been premeditated and that Erdemovic had not been responsible because he was under extreme duress.

"The judges have adjourned the hearing to make their decision after listening to the merits and demerits of the appeal," a tribunal spokeswoman said. "There is no set time for them to deliver a decision."
